title: Test-Retest Reliability of Safety Benchmarks Under Temperature Variation

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: unreliable benchmarks lead to inconsistent safety scores which undermine deployment decisions. Every link is explicit and defensible, with direct regulatory implications.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Running models at different temperatures on existing benchmarks is doable with standard API tools, public datasets, and Colab Pro. Statistical analysis of reliability coefficients is standard.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly focused: pick 2-3 benchmarks, 3-5 open-source models, run at multiple temperatures and seeds. Clear deliverable is a reliability coefficients table with recommendations.

novelty.reasoning: This idea is directly addressed by 'The Instability of Safety: How Random Seeds and Temperature Expose Inconsistent LLM Refusal Behavior' (arxiv 2512.12066, published Dec 2025). That paper systematically studies how temperature and random seeds affect safety refusal consistency, reports test-retest reliability metrics (97.7% at t=0.0, 92.4% pooled), identifies borderline prompts, and recommends at least 3 samples per prompt. The proposed study is essentially already completed.
